account:
Today I have repeatedly heard townsfolk mention a possible bridge or port change discussed at the bakery, naming baker, freight and neighbour. I have not witnessed that discussion or any actual crossing change. The secretary reports that baker described ordinary freight business and offered no firsthand evidence of crossing changes; the neighbour's story remains unverified. Reports of baker carrying bread and wheat, and freight carrying bread at the inn, may simply reflect deliveries. They do not establish a secret plan, though the repeated crossing story makes me want a firsthand explanation.

My mill appointment revealed 128 hay bales at the stall, equivalent to 1,152 wheat, but I have not established who manages the mill or checked its storage and deliveries. Baker apparently does not know the keeper. That is unfinished town business, not evidence of wrongdoing.

Builder reports no visible defects on the bridge and public-lighting routes he inspected, including the approaches, plaza, bakery street, warehouse route and landing. His inspection was neither a structural survey nor a nighttime lighting test. He reports no repairs, purchases or charges. I gave secretary two emeralds for writing supplies so his findings and their limits can be recorded. Today's council letters have not yet been located or presented to me.

I have now arrived at the east-bank cottage for my scheduled tea, a little late, and neighbour is waiting nearby. My next priority is to hear what neighbour actually knows: what change was discussed, who proposed it, and whether it was a proposal, ordinary delivery arrangements, or merely a rumour. At present ordinary freight business is a plausible explanation; I do not know of any concealed purpose.
